text: In the hills of the Dominican Republic, small farms grow much of the country's food. But pests and diseases can take up to forty percent of a harvest, and where the signal stops, help is far away.
Meet Conuco: a field assistant for those farmers, on the web in Chrome and as a native Android app. It turns the weather into clear daily decisions, and it keeps working offline.

Conuco is built on Firebase. Firebase AI Logic runs hybrid inference: Gemini Nano on the device first, and Gemini in the cloud only when it helps. Remote Config tunes the confidence floor and the models, live. Authentication and Firestore keep every farm log private and offline-first. And App Check, with Play Integrity and reCAPTCHA Enterprise, protects every AI call.
Now, the crop doctor. On Android, the big camera button opens a leaf camera, with a frame and live checks for blur and light, before the photo is taken.

On a laptop with Gemini Nano, Chrome runs the diagnosis right on the device. The photo is redrawn first, so location and camera data are gone. Nano answers with an honest confidence. On this device, the photo never left.
This phone has no Gemini Nano, so Conuco asks before anything leaves. With a yes, Gemini in the cloud answers in seconds: Black Sigatoka, severe, ninety-five percent.

Every step becomes a task with one tap. The advice is filtered: no pesticide doses, and a reminder to check with an extension officer. One tap warns the neighbours: the report lands on the outbreak map as an eleven-kilometre area, never a farm. And each morning, Today turns it all into one clear decision.
Conuco. The device first, the cloud only with consent, on the web and on Android. Built with Firebase, for the farmers where the signal stops. Try it today at petiht dot com slash conuco.
